Summary: The FOMC kept the federal funds rate unchanged at 4-1/4 to 4-1/2 percent and will continue balance-sheet runoff (Treasuries and agency MBS). The statement characterizes growth as solid, unemployment low, and inflation somewhat elevated, while noting uncertainty has diminished but remains elevated. The Committee maintains a risk‑management posture, monitoring incoming data and prepared to adjust policy if needed. Operational settings (IORB at 4.4%, ON RRP at 4.25%, standing repo at 4.5%) are consistent with a still‑restrictive stance.

SLOOS lens (April 2025): 
- C&I: Large banks reported largely unchanged standards, but “other banks” tightened standards and foreign banks tightened terms. Banks reported changes to credit lines, reflecting caution. 
- CRE: Banks tightened standards for CRE lending, and both large and foreign banks reported weaker demand for CRE loans. 
- Demand/credit appetite: Banks reported weaker customer financing needs and investment demand; reasons cited included economic outlook, supervisory actions, risk tolerance, and industry‑specific issues.

Implications for tone: While the macro language leans modestly hawkish, the SLOOS shows tighter credit supply and weaker loan demand—especially in CRE—with some tightening in C&I outside the largest institutions. These credit headwinds temper the hawkishness and support policy patience. Net tone: mildly positive/restrictive but less aggressively so once bank lending conditions are considered.
